summary: Kristin Johnston Largen is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. In 2018, she held posts as Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary and Associate Dean of Religious and Spiritual Life at Gettysburg College.

Kristin Scheible is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned a BA from Colby College and an MTS from Harvard University, studying under Anne E. Monius, Diana L. Eck, John S. Strong, and Charles Hallisey, later teaching at Harvard, Brown, and Bard College.

Kristina Myrvold works in religious studies and Indology. She was a redaktör and doctoral candidate at Lund University (attested 2005, 2008) and served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Linnaeus University (attested 2014).

Kristofer Schipper (1934–2021) was a Sinologist and religious studies scholar. Educated in Paris and Taiwan, he held posts at EFEO, EPHE (1972–2002), CNRS, Collège de France, Leiden University, and in China at Fuzhou and Minnan Normal universities.

Krisztina Teleki (born 1978) is a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at Eötvös Loránd University (1997–2009), where she also served as a research fellow around 2010.
Kshanika Saha is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Nalinaksha Dutt and earned her PhD from the University of Calcutta (attested 1966).
Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya (1896–1974) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ganganatha Jha. He held an academic post at the University of Allahabad (attested in 1933 and 1957).

Kshetreśachandra Chattopadhyaya (1896–1974) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Presidency, Allahabad, Calcutta, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit universities under Ganganatha Jha, he served as professor at the University of Allahabad (1924–1956) and directed the Research Institute at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Kshitimohan Sen (1880–1960) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He completed an MA in Sanskrit at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, worked in the Chamba State Education Department (1902–1908), and served as Adhyaksha at Visva-Bharati University (1953–1954).

Kumar Shrestha is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. In 2018, he was affiliated with the National Archives of Nepal and served as an editorial board member for the Documenta Nepalica Book Series.

Kumataro Kawada (1899–1981) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Tokyo Imperial University, he taught at Japan Women's University, Tokyo University of Literature and Science, the University of Tokyo (1950–1959), and became professor emeritus at Komazawa University.

Kumja Paik Kim (born 1934) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her doctorate from Stanford University and became curator of Korean art at the Asian Art Museum in 1989.

Kumkum Bandyopadhyay specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Rupendra Kumar Chattopadhyay and has held a post as a research scholar and fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Kun Chang (1917–2017) was a linguist, Sinologist, and Tibetologist. He studied at Tsinghua and Yale, where he earned his doctorate under Franklin Edgerton, and held faculty positions at the University of Washington and UC Berkeley (1963–1987).

Kunio Harikai (born 1942) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned his BA and PhD degrees from Kyushu University under Seiren Matsunami and Shōren Ihara, later serving as associate professor at Saga University and Saga Medical School.
Kunio Iwaya (born 1943) studied at the University of Tokyo between 1962 and 1970. He later held an academic post at Meiji Gakuin University from around 1970 to 2014.
Kunio Mugitani (born 1948) is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied under Mitsuji Fukunaga and served as a professor at Kyoto University from around 1992 to 2012.

Kunio Odaka (1908–1993) studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1928 to 1931. He subsequently held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (c. 1947–1969) and Sophia University (c. 1969–1979).

Kunio Yanagita (1875–1962) was a Japanese scholar of Japanology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Tokyo in law and politics, he held posts at the Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce, Tokyo Asahi Shimbun, and Kokugakuin University.

Kuno Fischer (1824–1907) was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg. He held professorships at the University of Jena (c. 1856–1872) and Heidelberg University (c. 1872–1906).
